title: A die at command-substitution depth 2 is swallowed, because inherit_errexit is set nowhere
body:
Command substitution does not inherit `errexit` unless `shopt -s inherit_errexit` is set, and that shopt appears NOWHERE in this repository. The consequence is narrow but exact: **a `die` reached at command-substitution depth 2 or deeper is swallowed** -- it prints its message, kills only its own subshell, and the caller reads an empty string and carries on.

**Depth 1 is SAFE, and that is measured rather than assumed.** `x="$(f)"` where `f` dies propagates fine, because the assignment's own status is 1 and the enclosing frame still has errexit. Two live probes on 2026-09-07, both `rc=1` and both correct:

- `infra mail dmarc parse` against a report with a non-numeric `date_range/begin` -- refused.
- `infra mail dmarc parse` against a record whose `dkim/domain` contains the `|` field separator, which reaches `auth_array`'s own `die` -- refused.

**Depth 2 is where it is lost**, ie a function called inside `$( )` that ITSELF substitutes a dying function. One live instance, found by walking into it while preparing the 0.1.1 release:

`bin/.devbin/cmd/release`, `note_when()` -> `note_status()`. A release note carrying no `status:` field made `note_status` print its refusal TWICE and `release notes` then **wrote both generated views and exited 0**, with the date rendered as though the note were released. The refusal was firing and being discarded. **FIXED** in that file with `shopt -s inherit_errexit`, covered by a new arm asserting the views are ABSENT (the message was already being printed, so an arm reading only the output would have passed throughout), and mutation-killed by reverting the shopt.

**What is still exposed, and it is smaller than a first count suggests.** A sweep of `lib/` found 44 functions that can die and 8 of them called inside `$( )`, but applying the depth-2 criterion leaves:

| Site | Shape | Assessment |
| ---- | ----- | ---------- |
| `lib/cmd/infra.d/mail.d/dmarc` | `auth_array()` -> `xq()` | Structural. NOT triggerable that I could find: the XPath is built from numeric indices against a document `xmllint --noout` has already accepted. |
| `lib/cmd/infra.d/mail.d/dmarc` | `auth_array()` -> `as_num()` | Structural. NOT triggerable: the value is a `count()`, always numeric. |
| `lib/help` | `cmd_meta()`, `opt_meta()`, `option_origin()` -> `resolve_handler()` | NOT a defect -- all three are `if handler="$(...)"` or `|| handler=""`, ie deliberately absorbing the failure. |

So: one live instance, fixed; two structural and unreachable today; three that are correct as written. **The reason to file rather than close is that unreachable-today is a property of the current callers, not of the code** -- the dmarc pair becomes live the moment `xq` or `as_num` is called from a new depth-2 position, and nothing would report it.

**THE FIX SHAPE IS A DECISION, NOT AN OBVIOUS PATCH, and it is why this is an issue rather than a commit.** `shopt -s inherit_errexit` in `bin/devbin` would close the whole class in one line -- and `bin/devbin` is VENDORED, so that line is in force across fourteen estates the moment it is committed, with no window in which to announce it. It also changes the failure behaviour of every existing command at once, including paths that may be relying on a swallowed failure without anyone knowing. The per-command form (as applied to `release`) is safe and slow. hv's standing directive on fleet blast radius applies to the dispatcher form; it does not apply to the per-command form.

bash >= 5 is the floor (issue 0022) and `inherit_errexit` is 4.4+, so availability is not a constraint either way.



## Measured 2026-09-14 -- what a one-line form actually reaches, and the one thing it broke

hv approved measuring before ruling. The run was a throwaway clone of devbin at `416a2e2`, never this tree, with exactly one line added: `shopt -s inherit_errexit` in `lib/helpers`, directly after its load guard.

**Why `lib/helpers` and not `bin/devbin`.** Handlers are reached by `exec` as separate bash processes, so a shell option set in the dispatcher does not reach them -- and the depth-2 sites this issue names, `auth_array` in `lib/cmd/infra.d/mail.d/dmarc`, are inside a handler. Every handler that can die sources `lib/helpers` itself, and so does the dispatcher, which makes that file the one place a single line reaches both. **So "one line in bin/devbin closes the whole class" is not true as written above: that form covers the dispatcher's own process only.** The `lib/helpers` form also changes a stated contract: the file says it "sets no shell options (the dispatcher owns those)".

**Result: 1057 of 1058, rc 1 captured directly after bats, no stray output.** The one failure is not a change in errexit behaviour. It is "a missing resolver is ONE error naming the tool, not one row per domain" in `tests/unit/infra-check.bats`, which builds a PATH out of `/usr/bin` and `/bin` so that `dig` is absent. On that PATH `#!/usr/bin/env bash` resolves to macOS's bash 3.2.57, and the added line dies at load with `shopt: inherit_errexit: invalid shell option name` before the handler does anything. **The bash >= 5 floor is enforced on the dispatcher's own interpreter; a handler exec'd under a narrower PATH can still run on 3.2, and the suite already does it.**

**The options this leaves for the ruling, stated without a recommendation:**

- **One line in `lib/helpers`, guarded by version** so it is set only where the shell has it. Closes the class for every handler on bash >= 4.4, changed no test verdict in this measurement, and leaves a handler reached on 3.2 exactly as exposed as today.
- **The same line unguarded.** A handler reached on 3.2 becomes a hard failure at load. Loud, and shown above to be reachable.
- **Per command, as `bin/.devbin/cmd/release` already does.** No fleet blast radius; the class stays open wherever nobody adds the line.

Either `lib/helpers` form is vendored, so it reaches every estate at its next upgrade and the pre-notice reservation on fleet-blast-radius changes applies to it.



## Ruled 2026-09-16 -- option A, after 0.1.1 is tagged

hv took vc's recommendation at 16:32Z: **one line in `lib/helpers`, guarded by bash version.** It lands after 0.1.1 is tagged and is announced before the next fleet sweep, because `lib/helpers` is vendored. The file's own "sets no shell options (the dispatcher owns those)" contract changes in the same commit.

**What the measurement did not cover, stated so the landing re-measures it.** cc's run was devbin's own suite. Estates' project handlers source `lib/helpers` too, and one of them may be relying on a swallowed failure; that has not been looked at.

**The 3.2 case has its own issue, 0076.** vc confirmed on 2026-09-16 that it is reachable through the dispatcher, and not only by running a handler directly: `env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin /opt/homebrew/bin/bash bin/devbin <cmd>` runs the handler on bash 3.2.57 with no refusal. If 0076 moves the floor check into `lib/helpers`, the version guard this ruling adds has nothing left to guard, so the two are best landed together.


---

## Fixed 2026-09-16 -- option A, landed with 0076 (vc), reviewed by dc

**Commit:** `acddd4d`.

`shopt -s inherit_errexit` is set in `lib/helpers`, directly after the load guard. It has NO version guard, because 0076 put the floor ahead of it in the same file, and every bash below 5 is refused before the line is reached. The file's "sets no shell options" contract is rewritten to say it sets exactly this one. `bin/.devbin/cmd/release` dropped its own copy; its arm asserting the views are ABSENT now holds the line in `lib/helpers`.

**Arm:** a `die` two substitutions deep stops the caller (`tests/unit/helpers.bats`).

**Mutation check:** removing the shopt turns that arm red, along with release's no-status arm. The suite is 1150/1150 at `acddd4d`.

**Blast radius -- pre-notice owed to hv before the next sweep.** `lib/helpers` is vendored, so estates get this at their next upgrade. Their own `cmd/` handlers that source `lib/helpers` inherit `inherit_errexit`: a `$( )` whose non-final command fails now aborts that substitution where it used to carry on. cc's measurement covered devbin's suite only. Before the sweep, run the suites of the estates with the most shell handlers, so the effect is measured rather than assumed.
